title: General Pulaski Memorial Day, 2025
summary:
The President has proclaimed October 11, 2025 as General Pulaski Memorial Day, honoring Casimir Pulaski, a Polish-born hero of the American Revolution known for shaping the early American cavalry and sacrificing his life for the cause of independence.

The proclamation retells Pulaski’s journey from fighting for freedom in Poland to joining the American struggle at Benjamin Franklin’s urging. It highlights his daring role at the Battle of Brandywine, his leadership as a brigadier general, and his death after being wounded at the Siege of Savannah. It also frames his story as a lasting bond between Poland and the United States, and ties this remembrance to the approaching 250th anniversary of American independence. The message encourages Americans to commemorate those who have strengthened the nation through service and sacrifice.

This recognition benefits Polish-American communities, veterans and military families, educators, civic groups, and local leaders who organize observances and use these moments to teach and reflect on shared history. It may also support cultural and diplomatic ties between Poland and the United States by spotlighting a figure respected in both countries.

Some may view the proclamation as largely symbolic, preferring attention to present-day challenges or a broader range of historical voices. Others might be uneasy with celebratory language that can gloss over complex histories or worry that such observances can feel exclusive when many communities seek recognition. As with most commemorations, it may prompt debate over which figures are highlighted and how national memory is shaped.
